import asyncio, time

async def fetch(name, delay):
    print(f"    {name} starts")
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)          # yields control here
    print(f"    {name} done after {delay}s")
    return f"{name}-result"

async def sequential():
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    a = await fetch("A", 0.3)
    b = await fetch("B", 0.3)
    return time.monotonic() - t0, [a, b]

async def concurrent():
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    results = await asyncio.gather(fetch("A", 0.3), fetch("B", 0.3))
    return time.monotonic() - t0, results

async def main():
    print("=== Awaiting one after the other ===")
    elapsed, results = await sequential()
    print(f"  elapsed {elapsed:.2f}s  {results}")

    print("\n=== Awaiting both together ===")
    elapsed, results = await concurrent()
    print(f"  elapsed {elapsed:.2f}s  {results}")

    print("\nOne thread, two tasks. The second run is not faster because")
    print("it used two CPUs; it is faster because A's WAIT overlapped B's.")

asyncio.run(main())
description: Async functions use await to pause at sleep points. Sequential awaits one after another, concurrent uses gather to overlap waits.

steps.description: fetch is an async function that prints start, awaits a sleep, prints done, and returns a result string.
sequential awaits fetch A then fetch B, measuring total elapsed time. Each await pauses until complete.
concurrent uses asyncio.gather to await both fetches together, allowing their wait times to overlap.
main runs sequential and concurrent, printing elapsed times and results for each.
